findings.problem: The hint 'bring people or things together' fits juntar equally well, and juntar is very common in Latin America (juntar a la familia, juntar dinero), so the prompt has two right answers.
findings.fix: hint: bring people together, as for a reunion (not juntar)

back.es: to gather, to bring together, to collect (transitive)
back.example: My grandmother gets the whole family together at Christmas.

note: The forms reúno, reúnes and reúne only add a written accent, so irregular: false holds up, but the accent is easy to miss and a learner may need it pointed out.
